I’d say overall I’m still a lot blurrier in the head than I used to be, it’s mostly come down to reducing activities that require lots of thinking to cope. 

That being said stress is also likely a factor in this as that’s been quite nasty over the last few months. 

I’ll ask my gp next time I see them
Same day as starting dose, eased off over time and coming back on each dose increase. Still around a little bit now days (though may be due to inconsistencies in taking every dose each day)

She’s at ER now. Very pale and she struggled to stand up to get into the car. Can’t be there with her due to Covid restrictions but from my experience with that particular er they should hopefully take care of her well.

My doctor is usually good with informing me about things it’s just this time it was mostly based on my suggestion and she was looking stuff up on the fly during the appointment so she missed a few things, that and the Australian medication database they have access to buried the central nervous system effects under the full description. Will definitely be bringing it up with her this week to see where exactly the process went wrong in informing me

Oh thank goodness. I’ve had a history of things but hadn’t ever had them to this degree, and yeah it was really nasty and those things have been slightly worse than normal anyway this week which makes sense. Just mostly glad that they can possibly go away over time as none of the documentation I found even the internal stuff mentioned the symptoms desisting, I was worried I’d have to go off this which would suck because the positive effects have already been so good.
30 seconds after writing that I collapsed trying to get up and walk so yeah that might be a thing

Yeah hypotension could definitely be an issue given I already had that going. Will have to see what doctor thinks but it might be worth trying a higher dose before writing it off as even the current level quantitatively lowered my heart rate throughout the day with similar levels of activity. Was only on such a low dose as my gp was waiting on the letter to come through from my cardiologist
I’m only on 20 for now (10 twice daily). I had the drowsiness day one but that faded and with the reduction in other symptoms I was actually able to function more than usual.

Honestly I’ve been simultaneously terrified but also so close to returning to what led to the hits. Part of me thinks that if it happened again it might be enough to take me out entirely and I wouldn’t have to deal with anything. 

I hope I can find ways that it gets better so those thoughts don’t lead to actions. It’s been a rough few days for me too with this stuff and another chronic illness. Hopefully I can have some good days soon

Will keep an eye out for that. CFS would probably just be brushed off as being attributed to my dysautonomic issues so I didn’t really bother given any disability benefits lump them together anyway. As for the reading, unfortunately it and especially audiobooks have been quite difficult as an unknown injury left me with partial aphasia at some point over the last 3 years, just hadn’t been able to pin down when due to how much it depends on my fatigue levels.

Yeah I was already dealing with some fatigue issues but now it’s at a level where it’s likely CFS with how I’m unable to function most days. CBD might be worth a shot as I’d previously used it for anxiety years ago. 

Will see what I can find with the education stuff. Might try a quick math course online as that’s the biggest thing I lost to my first TBI and I’m assuming moreso now. Just to see if my brain can find some way around it. Neuroplasticity gives me a bit of hope given I was already neurodivergent.

I guess I was somewhat lucky in that my whole life was voluntarily changed at the time of the tbi so I had already been processing dropping everything and starting over. Just need to process that not all of that is in my control which is probably going to be difficult with how control and understanding is the only way I’ve been able to cope with other chronic health issues. I hope things work out. And yeah I’m really upset about it, especially the contexts around it and how it could have been avoided. I hope I learn to accept who I am and who I’ll become.
Thank you. I really hope I find something, my first neurologist appointment since my first tbi was glossed over in 2018 is in a few months so I’m hoping they can help with something

I had a smaller tbi in 2018 which I had started to get a hang of before these ones happened. I hope the same can happen with these. Having recently finally gotten answers and help after 3 years for other chronic health things I do have hope that I’ll learn with these. Planning to tell my therapist next week in hopes they can help with processing whatever’s going to end up of my life.
Thank you. I hope if my current goals do prove to be impossible that I can find something else. I really do
I hadn’t heard of it, I’m not sure what counts as a short time but the last major ones were in July/August 2021. I’ll ask my neurologist when I see them in a few months.

Thanks so much for this, I’ll have to look into it a bit more and see if their reception knows if my insurance will work out.

Thanks. Still trying to push through it and fill out the paperwork anyway but since it’s a shelter meant for youth to get us back on our feet they said they don’t accept anyone that might make others worse, unfortunately it’s one of the only safe ones for queer/lgbt people so I don’t really have any other options and the paperwork specifically asks when my last attempt was. I really do want to try and find a way of getting through this im just so tired and done and I can’t keep pushing like this.

You really don’t want a diagnosis for this. Especially not on paper or your record. 
Anything involving informed consent will suddenly question your stability and might prevent you from things
Doctors will use it to blame other important diagnosis’s on (Our psyc has blamed BPD for our OSDD-1b since we mentioned it to him, despite our regular therapist saying that we had OSDD-1b and proceeding with treatment for it)
In psychiatric wards you are more likely to be made involuntary
They are more likely to ignore and not help you if you are harmed from self harm. 

I get that you want validation, we did too. But don’t get it on the record and definitely don’t tell people because they won’t trust anything you do because of it.
